name: Elijah
summary: The prophet who confronted Ahab and the prophets of Baal in 1 Kings; here he announces Ahaziah's death, calls down fire on two captains of fifty, and is taken up to heaven in a whirlwind, leaving his mantle to Elisha.

name: Elisha
summary: Elijah's successor and Israel's prophet through most of this book; he performs miracles for the poor and powerful alike, advises kings, and even his bones revive a dead man after his death.

name: Ahaziah
summary: Ahab's son and king of Israel; after a fall leaves him injured, he inquires of the god of Ekron rather than the LORD and dies as Elijah foretold, leaving no son to succeed him.

name: Joram
summary: Ahab's second son and king of Israel; he campaigns against Moab with Elisha's help, is wounded fighting Hazael, and is shot dead by Jehu on Naboth's old plot of ground.

name: Jehoshaphat
summary: King of Judah who joins Israel's campaign against Moab and, because of his own faithfulness, is the reason Elisha agrees to help the allied kings at all.

name: Mesha
summary: King of Moab who rebels against Israel after Ahab's death; when his desperate breakout fails during the siege of Kir-hareseth, he sacrifices his own son as a burnt offering on the city wall.

name: The Shunammite woman
summary: A wealthy woman of Shunem who hosts Elisha regularly and is given a room for him; Elisha promises and later raises her son from death, and years afterward the king restores her land after a famine.

name: Gehazi
summary: Elisha's servant who fails to revive the Shunammite's son with Elisha's staff, later secretly extorts payment from the healed Naaman, and is struck with Naaman's leprosy for his deceit.

name: Naaman
summary: Commander of Syria's army who is healed of leprosy after washing seven times in the Jordan at Elisha's word, and afterward confesses that the LORD alone is God.

name: Ben-hadad
summary: King of Syria who besieges Samaria until famine breaks the city; later, sick and near death, he is murdered by his own officer Hazael, who takes the throne.

name: Hazael
summary: A Syrian officer whom Elisha foresees will become king and inflict great cruelty on Israel; he murders Ben-hadad to take the throne and goes on to oppress Israel and threaten Judah for decades.

name: Jehoram
summary: King of Judah who marries into Ahab's family and walks in the evil ways of Israel's kings; Edom revolts from Judah's rule during his reign.

name: Ahaziah of Judah
summary: Jehoram's son and king of Judah, related by marriage to Ahab's house; he is fatally wounded fleeing Jehu after visiting the injured Joram of Israel at Jezreel.

name: Jehu
summary: An army commander secretly anointed king of Israel and commissioned to destroy Ahab's house; he kills Joram, Ahaziah, and Jezebel, wipes out Ahab's remaining family, and tricks Baal's worshipers into a fatal assembly, though he never abandons Jeroboam's golden calves.

name: Jezebel
summary: Ahab's widow, still in Jezreel when Jehu arrives; she taunts him from a window and is thrown down at his order, her body eaten by dogs as Elijah had prophesied.

name: Jehonadab
summary: Son of Rechab who joins Jehu's chariot to witness his zeal for the LORD, riding with him into Samaria during the purge of Baal worship.

name: Athaliah
summary: Ahaziah's mother, of Ahab's house, who destroys the rest of Judah's royal family and rules for six years until Jehoiada crowns the hidden Joash and has her put to death.

name: Jehosheba
summary: Ahaziah's sister who steals away the infant Joash during Athaliah's purge and hides him with his nurse in the temple for six years.

name: Jehoiada
summary: The priest who protects Joash in hiding, then arms the temple guard and crowns Joash king in Athaliah's place; he later instructs Joash and sets up the chest that funds the temple's repair.

name: Joash
summary: Judah's king from age seven, crowned after Athaliah's coup and instructed by Jehoiada; he repairs the temple through an honest collection chest but later strips it to pay off Hazael and is assassinated by his own servants.

name: Jehoahaz
summary: King of Israel whose army is reduced to almost nothing by Syrian oppression; he seeks the LORD's favor and receives some relief, but Israel's underlying sin continues.

name: Jehoash
summary: King of Israel who weeps over the dying Elisha and receives his prophecy of three victories over Syria; he later defeats Amaziah of Judah in battle and breaks down part of Jerusalem's wall.

name: Amaziah
summary: King of Judah who defeats Edom but, made proud by victory, provokes Jehoash of Israel into a battle that leaves Judah routed and Jerusalem's wall broken; he is later assassinated after fleeing to Lachish.

name: Jeroboam II
summary: King of Israel whose long reign restores Israel's borders to their widest extent, fulfilling a word the LORD spoke through the prophet Jonah.

name: Azariah
summary: Also called Uzziah, king of Judah who reigns fifty-two years but is struck with leprosy and lives apart, leaving his son Jotham to govern the people.

name: Jotham
summary: Azariah's son who governs Judah while his leprous father lives apart, and later succeeds him as king.

name: Zechariah
summary: Jeroboam II's son and king of Israel for six months before Shallum assassinates him, ending Jehu's dynasty exactly at the fourth generation the LORD had promised.

name: Shallum
summary: Assassinates Zechariah and reigns over Israel for just one month before Menahem kills him and takes the throne.

name: Menahem
summary: Kills Shallum and reigns brutally over Israel for ten years, at one point ripping open pregnant women in a conquered town; he pays off the Assyrian king Pul with silver exacted from Israel's wealthy.

name: Pekahiah
summary: Menahem's son and king of Israel for two years before his own captain Pekah murders him in the citadel of the royal palace.

name: Pekah
summary: Assassinates Pekahiah and reigns twenty years over Israel while Assyria's Tiglath-pileser conquers large stretches of Israelite territory; Hoshea later conspires against him and takes the throne.

name: Ahaz
summary: King of Judah who, besieged by Syria and Israel, strips the temple treasury to buy Assyria's help and later copies a pagan altar he saw in Damascus for use in the temple.

name: Hoshea
summary: The last king of Israel; his rebellion against Assyria and appeal to Egypt bring a three-year siege that ends with Samaria's fall and Israel's exile.

name: Hezekiah
summary: King of Judah whose trust in the LORD is unmatched by any king before or after him; he survives Sennacherib's siege through prayer, is healed of a fatal illness, but is later warned that his pride before Babylonian envoys foreshadows Judah's own exile.

name: Sennacherib
summary: King of Assyria who invades Judah, besieges Jerusalem after collecting tribute, and loses 185,000 soldiers to the angel of the LORD before being assassinated by his own sons at home.

name: The Rabshakeh
summary: Sennacherib's officer who stands outside Jerusalem's wall and mocks Hezekiah's trust in the LORD, urging the people to surrender rather than believe the LORD can save them.

name: Isaiah
summary: The prophet who reassures Hezekiah during Sennacherib's siege, promises the Assyrian army's defeat, and later both heals and warns Hezekiah about his illness and his pride before Babylon's envoys.

name: Manasseh
summary: Hezekiah's son and king of Judah for fifty-five years; his idolatry, child sacrifice, and shedding of innocent blood provoke the LORD's irreversible sentence of judgment on Jerusalem.

name: Amon
summary: Manasseh's son and king of Judah for two evil years before his own servants assassinate him in his house.

name: Josiah
summary: Amon's son and king of Judah from age eight; he orders the temple repaired, hears the newly found Book of the Law, leads Judah's last great reform and Passover, and dies in battle against Pharaoh Neco at Megiddo.

name: Hilkiah
summary: The high priest who discovers the Book of the Law in the temple during Josiah's repairs and has it read to the king.

name: Huldah
summary: A prophetess Josiah's officials consult about the newly found Book of the Law; she confirms disaster is coming on Jerusalem but promises Josiah he will die in peace first.

name: Jehoahaz
summary: Josiah's son, made king by the people of Judah after his father's death, but deposed by Pharaoh Neco after just three months and taken captive to Egypt.

name: Jehoiakim
summary: Installed as king of Judah by Pharaoh Neco in place of his brother Jehoahaz; he later becomes Nebuchadnezzar's servant for three years before rebelling.

name: Jehoiachin
summary: Jehoiakim's son who reigns only three months before surrendering Jerusalem to Nebuchadnezzar and being deported to Babylon; decades later a new Babylonian king frees him from prison and honors him at his own table.

name: Zedekiah
summary: Jehoiachin's uncle, installed as king of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar and renamed from Mattaniah; his later rebellion brings Jerusalem's final siege, and he is captured, blinded, and taken to Babylon after watching his sons killed.

name: Nebuchadnezzar
summary: King of Babylon who subdues Jehoiakim, deports Jehoiachin, installs and later punishes Zedekiah's rebellion by destroying Jerusalem and its temple.

name: Gedaliah
summary: Appointed governor over Judah's remaining people after Jerusalem's fall; he is assassinated within months by Ishmael, a member of the royal family, prompting many survivors to flee to Egypt.
